title: Educational: how risk factors affect arteries
label: General education — not patient-specific, not from this model
note: These are general-population facts from public health sources. They do not change this patient's estimate, the colours on the heart, or any location on it.

items.title: Smoking
items.text: Smoking damages the inner lining of the arteries and promotes plaque build-up and blood clots. It is estimated to raise the risk of coronary heart disease by 2 to 4 times; risk falls after quitting.
items.source: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC): Health Effects of Cigarette Smoking

items.title: High blood pressure
items.text: Persistently high blood pressure strains and damages artery walls over time and is one of the leading modifiable risk factors for heart attack and stroke.
items.source: World Health Organization (WHO): Hypertension fact sheet

items.title: Diabetes
items.text: Over time, high blood sugar can damage blood vessels and the nerves that control the heart. Adults with diabetes are about twice as likely to have heart disease or a stroke as adults without diabetes.
items.source: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC): Diabetes and Your Heart

items.title: LDL cholesterol
items.text: LDL cholesterol contributes to fatty plaque (atherosclerosis) in artery walls. Lowering LDL cholesterol lowers the risk of cardiovascular events.
items.source: 2019 ESC/EAS Guidelines for the management of dyslipidaemias (Mach F. et al., Eur Heart J 2020;41:111-188)
